reading.title: Smart Choices with Money
reading.purpose: Learn basic money habits that help people plan, save, and avoid owing too much.
paras: Whether you earn five dollars walking a neighbor's dog or run a busy bakery, good money habits work the same way. You do not have to be wealthy, with piles of riches, to make wise choices.

Start by listing your income, the money you earn or receive each week. Next, list every regular expense, the money you must spend on supplies, bus fare, or snacks. Putting those two lists together gives you a budget, a clear plan for how to spend and save.

People who are thrifty are careful not to waste money. Before you purchase a new jacket or backpack, check whether you can really afford it with the cash you have saved. Sometimes waiting for a sale helps you find a real bargain, an item that costs much less than it is worth.

Borrowing money creates debt, money you owe and must pay back later. Too much debt can make future months stressful. Small businesses watch these numbers closely too: after paying for ingredients and rent, the money left over is their profit.
A clear plan turns small coins into steady savings over time.

choices: the cash left over after a bakery pays its rent
a clear plan for how to spend and save money
an item on sale that costs less than its value
money that you owe to a friend or a bank

qs.q: A small shop earns fifty dollars selling muffins and spends twenty dollars on flour and eggs. Which word from the reading names the thirty dollars left over?
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says that after paying for ingredients and rent, the money left over is profit.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only wealthy business owners need to write down a weekly spending plan.
Planning income, expenses, and savings helps anyone make smart money choices.
Walking a neighbor's dog pays better than running a small neighborhood bakery.
Waiting for a sale is the only way to keep from ever owing money later.
qs.why: The reading explains how budgets, thrift, avoiding excess debt, and tracking profit help people manage money wisely.
